sentences.text: Going to the supermarket is something we do every day. If you travel to an English-speaking country, you may need to buy food, ask for help, or pay at the cashier.
Supermarkets can be big and confusing, so it's important to know useful English phrases for shopping.
In this episode, I will teach you.
1. How to find a shopping cart or basket.
2. How to ask where things are.
3. How to talk to supermarket employees.
4. How to check prices and read labels.
5. How to pay at the cashier.
6. Extra useful words and phrases for shopping.
By the end of this episode, you will feel more confident speaking English at the supermarket.
Let's get started.
At the entrance, getting a shopping cart or basket.
When you enter the supermarket, you need a shopping cart or a basket.
A shopping cart is good if you are buying many items.
A shopping basket is good if you are buying just a few things.
If you need a cart, you can ask.
Excuse me, where can I get a shopping cart?
If you want a basket, you can say, do you have a shopping basket?
Some supermarkets require a coin to unlock a cart.
If you don't have one, you can ask, do I need a coin for the cart?
Where can I get a token for the shopping cart?
Now you are ready to start shopping.
Asking for help in the supermarket.
Sometimes, it is difficult to find the products you need.
You can ask a store employee for help.
Excuse me, where can I find the milk?
Where is the bread section?
Do you sell fresh fruit?
To ask if something is available?
Do you have almond milk?
Is there any gluten-free bread?
Do you sell organic eggs?
To ask about prices or sizes?
How much is this?
Do you have a smaller size?
Is there a discount on this?
Employees will be happy to help you.
Reading prices and labels.
In English-speaking countries, prices are written in dollars, pounds or euros.
Here's how to say prices.
Common supermarket labels.
Buy one, get one free.
Buy one, get a second one for free.
50% off, the item is half price.
Clearant sale, prices are very low.
Best before, the food is best before this date.
Used by, the food must be eaten before this date.
If you don't understand a label, you can ask, excuse me, what does bogo mean?
Can you explain this label to me?
Talking to the cashier.
After shopping, you go to the checkout counter to pay.
The cashier will usually greet you.
Hello, did you find everything okay?
You can answer, yes, thank you.
No, I couldn't find the flower.
Then the cashier will ask, do you need a bag?
Would you like a receipt?
If you brought your own bag, you can say, no, thank you.
I have my own bag.
If you need a plastic bag, you can ask, do you charge for bags?
The cashier will tell you the total price.
That will be $15.25.
You can ask, can I pay with a credit card?
Do you accept cash?
If the machine doesn't work, the cashier might say, could you try again please?
Do you have another card?
After paying, the cashier will say, here is your receipt.
Have a great day.
You can reply, thank you, you too.
Self-checkout machines.
Many supermarkets have self-checkout machines.
If you use a self-checkout machine, you must, one, scan your items.
Two, put them in the bagging area.
Three, pay with cash or a card.
If you need help, you can ask.
Excuse me, the machine isn't working.
How do I scan this item?
A staff member will help you.
Useful supermarket vocabulary.
Here are some important words and phrases to remember.
Types of food, dairy products, milk, cheese, yogurt, bakery, bread, cake cookies, fruits and vegetables, apples, bananas, carrots, meat and seafood, chicken, beef, fish,
frozen food, ice cream, frozen pizza, shopping phrases.
Where can I find the eggs?
How much does this cost?
Can I pay by card?
Do you have plastic bags?
Thank you.
Have a nice day.
Common store sections, aisle, a row of shelves in a supermarket, cash register, where you pay.
Checkout counter, where the cashier works.
Express lane, a fast checkout for 10 items or less.
Bargain, a product that is a good deal.
Now, you know how to speak English at the supermarket.
Next time you go shopping, try using some of these phrases.
Remember, practice makes perfect.
